A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Frankentexts work. All 42 pages of v3 and 40 pages of v4, including appendices, tables, figures and pseudocode, support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V3 reports original multi-model generation experiments, automatic detector results, human evaluations and supplementary experiments on fiction and news.

after.justification: V4 retains original generation and human-evaluation results and adds RAG, plagiarism-detection and writing-metric validation results.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline remains unchanged: snippet-based drafting, optional copy-rate revision and up to three polishing rounds. Algorithm 1 and the generation, editing and judging prompts match across versions. The added RAG baseline and diagnostic controls do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Generation coverage retains English Mythos/r/WritingPrompts, Tell Me a Story, news, single-book snippets and longer outputs. V4 adds a limited plagiarism-detection task on Frankentexts (Limitations, footnote 16), testing detection of copied material beyond the existing AI-authorship classification evaluations.

E2.justification: V4 adds an evaluated Gemini-2.5-Pro RAG baseline to Table 2 and a disjointed copied-span control to the writing-metric comparison in Table 22. V3's random-fragment WQRM control is retained separately. The five vanilla model baselines and existing AI detectors remain, while Pangram's plagiarism detector is additionally tested.

E3.justification: New protocols include retrieving 1,500 relevant Books3 paragraphs and removing copying requirements for RAG, constructing disjointed controls from exact copied n-grams, and testing plagiarism detection on 300 outputs, 100 per model. V4 also reports average copied-span length. The principal generation settings and human-study sample sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V4 substantially expands diagnostic validation with surprise–coherence analysis, tests of the main writing metrics on disjointed text, copied-span-length analysis and a plagiarism-detector probe. It adds a detailed error taxonomy and a case where vanilla writing is preferred (Tables 9 and 15). Existing editing, copy-rate, snippet-count, prompt-specificity and single-book ablations are retained.

E5.justification: V3 provides point estimates and agreement coefficients. V4 adds bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals for single-story, pairwise and automatic evaluations, specifying 10,000 bootstrap iterations for human annotations (Appendix B.4; Tables 10–12). It also adds Fleiss' kappa, label distributions, binary judgment correlations and a surprise–coherence significance test. These additions do not establish additional generation runs or larger samples.

E6.justification: Most matched benchmark scores are identical, but substantial diagnostic results are added: RAG scores 3.46 on the LLM judge with 2% classified as human; disjointed texts score 0.60 utility and 2.88 on the judge; plagiarism flagging rates are 10% for Gemini, 15% for GPT-5 and 21% for Claude. V4 also adds copied-span lengths, corrects cost totals, changes reported MCP usage from 15–20 to 3–5 calls, and removes two Figure 10 entries and the Section 4.3 error-frequency percentages.

T1.justification: The copy-rate construction and algorithmic specification remain unchanged. Neither version presents theoretical propositions or proofs, and the new empirical statistical analyses do not introduce substantive formal theory.

C1.justification: V4 narrows broad quality and coherence assertions to improvements in key writing metrics with mostly coherent outputs, and extends explicit comparison claims to RAG. It foregrounds black-box generation of high-quality, low-detectability narratives. The composer paradigm, diversity advantage and mixed-authorship-detection contribution remain.

C2.justification: V4 adds substantive interpretations distinguishing diversity from writing quality, explaining uncertainty and imbalanced-label agreement, and attributing weak agentic results to retrieval underuse and integration difficulties. Limitations and ethics expand to potential defenses, excluded humanization baselines, economic misuse feasibility and competing definitions of authorship. The MCP explanation remains internally inconsistent with Appendix G's account of calls without the retrieval constraint.

D1.justification: V4 replaces the first-page promise of a post-review release with a repository link, identifies Vertex and OpenRouter, and corrects cost summaries. It removes the stated 512-token judging limit, calibration using 2,700 MT-bench evaluations and explicit pairwise presentation randomization. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish that the omitted procedures ceased.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is largely retained. V4 adds references supporting detector-evasion and publishing concerns, including Cheng et al., Knibbs and Russell et al.'s newspaper study, plus agreement and sample-size context. Legal references including Ricketson, Mezzi et al. and the U.S. Copyright Office are removed. Publication updates and duplicate entries do not constitute new cited works.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion and limitations receive substantial rewriting around detector evasion and publishing risks. Appendices are reorganized, limitations and ethics move before the references, the co-writing discussion moves into Appendix D.4, and duplicated human-detection discussion is consolidated. These changes substantially revise the narrative and document structure.

P2.justification: V4 switches the body to two columns and extensively rearranges tables, figures and prompt displays. It adds nine tables, transposes and moves the agentic-results table into the main text, and transposes the agreement table. Figure 7's story is replaced and Figure 10 contracts from six model entries to four. The pipeline and human-rating figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: V4 improves evidential clarity through the RAG comparison, disjointed-text metric checks and confidence intervals absent from v3. Table 11 distinguishes supported language-use and overall-interest gains from less certain gains in other dimensions, while Table 22 clarifies the limits of diversity metrics. These benefits are tempered by contradictory MCP reporting and removed calibration and randomization details. Overall, the paper becomes better supported and qualified, with a limited net improvement.
